title: Short-term rental licensing deferred; municipal accommodation tax approved
subtitle: Also: shuttle bus funding, 2025 deficit, Bissell Park grant, planning permit system, alcohol framework, clerk retirement.
overview: Council deferred any further action on licensing short-term rentals and bed and breakfasts until the next term of Council {{vote:m10}}. Several delegates raised concerns about parking rules, costs, restrictions on family events and the process. Because the zoning amendment depended on the licensing by-law, it did not proceed either. Council also approved a Municipal Accommodation Tax by-law {{vote:m12}}, with the 5% rate and September 1, 2026 start date proposed by staff.

Council approved the 2026 Shuttle Bus Program between downtown Fergus and downtown Elora {{vote:m5}}. It covered the 2025 operating deficit of $51,433 from the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve {{vote:m4}}. It also endorsed an accessibility grant application for the Bissell Park multi-use pad {{vote:m6}} and chose not to opt in to Ontario's bring-your-own alcohol framework for outdoor events {{vote:m9}}.

On the Community Planning Permit System, Council only received the staff report, so staff will refine the scope before any consultant is hired {{vote:m7}}. Council also thanked retiring Clerk Kerri O'Kane for over 20 years of service {{vote:m15}}, and the consent agenda appointed a new Clerk and Fire Chief {{vote:m3}}. No matters came out of closed session.

decisions.detail: Council received the update report and deferred further action on licensing short-term rentals and bed and breakfasts until the new term of Council.
Council received the update report and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to execute a by-law establishing a Municipal Accommodation Tax.
Council directed staff to proceed with the 2026 shuttle between downtown Fergus and Elora, running May 15 to September 7.
Council received the report and directed a transfer of $51,433 from the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve to cover the 2025 deficit.
Council endorsed a 2026/2027 EASE grant application for the Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad Replacement and delegated authority to sign funding agreements if successful.
Council endorsed not opting in to the provincial framework for now and directed staff to monitor other municipalities and report back.
Council received the staff report for information only, without endorsing the proposed request for proposals, so staff can revise the scope.

debate: Delegates on short-term rentals said the process lacked transparency and notice. One said parking rules for downtown units could stop small owners from ever converting to short-term rental, and one asked for a further public meeting. Another asked that existing residential units above shops not become hotels without a zoning amendment.

Delegates who run bed and breakfasts raised licensing costs, the Municipal Accommodation Tax, and a clause barring parties and weddings. They said it could prevent family events and conflicts with the zoning by-law's occasional-use provision. Staff said personal family gatherings would not be enforced and that the clause could be removed.

On short-term rentals, councillors weighed staff workload and the election against the wish to move forward. After staff explained that the zoning change would take effect immediately, ahead of licensing, several councillors switched to deferral. Staff said changing the zoning would require a new public meeting.

On the planning permit system, one councillor said the proposed request for proposals went beyond a feasibility study, and asked for a phased approach and a committee-of-the-whole workshop. Others asked about effects on agriculture, heritage, water and reduced public meetings. Staff said the first phase could be a feasibility study and that Council would decide whether to proceed.

On the accommodation tax, one councillor preferred starting at 3.5% until the new service corporation's board could review it. Staff said 5% was needed to balance tourism and economic development funding and avoid revisiting the rate soon.
